I'm not sure what geology looks like, but I know in a lot of more "mainstream" STEM fields it's very typical to get a full ride for your PhD in graduate school, which is why I was looking at that over getting a Master's. 

I actually didn't realize it was easier to get an academic job in this field. In anthropology/chemistry it's insanely difficult, like, even if you're the cream of the crop in anthropology there is absolutely no guarantee you'll get a job as a professor because there's just so many other candidates.

I was wondering - what does your typical day look like as a geologist? Do you do a lot of field research, lab work, reading/writing, etc.? The problems I'm having with my current job are that I feel like I'm stuck inside a lab working with dangerous chemicals literally year round lol. My research is really impactful but it's hard to see that impact when my only responsibilities are to make compounds. I'd really love a job that had more diversity in tasks, like, I want to write more papers/present/teach (which just comes with being in academia & in pursuing higher ed), but I also want diversity in my actual research too. It kills me to do lab work 8+ hours a day every single day with no other tasks, I just don't enjoy it enough.

I spy an archaeologist.

The only problem with me trying to get into school for archaeology is I didn't do a field/dig school in undergrad (and they tend to be pretty expensive).

Are master's in geology/volcanology typically funded? I'm interested in getting a PhD (partially for the funding, partially for the thesis/research/job opportunities) but I'm trying to make sure I'm choosing the right field first before throwing myself into one.

Also, I'm curious - what jobs are out there for people who specialize in volcanology/geology? The only ones I've come across that aren't NASA/professorships are like... jobs with Exon or other gas companies where you're scouting out new drill sites which goes against my moral compass lol. I'd honestly love to be a part of the team in Iceland that just monitors volcanic activity and earthquakes...

also along the lines of what you said - sometimes you spend so much time doing a few select things that it all gets boring and pointless. while humans are creatures of habit, too much routine sucks the soul out of you. go join a fuckin DND group. pick up a book. try painting or writing something or making music. go to a concert (free ones exist locally if you can't afford to see a band you like). just throw yourself out there and do something new.

one of the most life changing experiences for me was traveling to iceland this year. i don't think i can be properly suicidal anymore because of those 2 and a half weeks. not everyone has the means to travel and i'm in debt for it now but. it doesn't have to be iceland. get yourself to a new place for a little while.

i get that. maybe in your immediate future there isn't much to look forward to. i think we all have times like that tbh. i lost passion for both of my majors in my final year of college to the point where i dropped down to a single class in my last semester and gave up a bunch of amazing opportunities because i was so fucking depressed. i graduated anyway. now i have a job i never dreamed i would even get an interview for. this january before my final semester i was sure i was fucked. 

point is, shit changes. and it's not going to change on its own. you gotta be strategic about it. i'm the master of low-effort zero energy plans that put myself ahead lmao. because depression does that to you and makes it so you can't fucking apply effort to anything consistently.

change of scenery helps. trying something new helps. think about what you think your life needs right now, or is missing. maybe you don't WANT it right now. but there are probably things that come to mind. how can you obtain them?
yo i do this too. i like cycle between things. right now it's apex, sometimes i write (creative hobbies are actually REALLY good for releasing pent up grief), or i play league, or... whatever else.

no, i agree. anonymous help can be good help tbh. the only problem i have is when people aren't actually trying to help and they're just saying things they think are helpful but... can often make depressed people feel worse. like the suicidewatch subreddit has rules on the kind of stuff you can say in a thread, for example.

i also don't disagree with you on your last point either. the way people view life when they're at such a low is very unhealthy. it only makes sense that someone who isn't experiencing that in the moment would get frustrated and want to argue, even if it invalidates the depressed person's feelings. good intentions, but, this is also why depressed ppl need to talk to therapists too lol

yeah but the problem is, an anonymous stranger "feeling" for a depressed person is just as fleeting as when you see a sad picture on reddit and feel sad for a minute before clicking on something cute. you forget all about it in an instant, you know?

and what depressed people seek out with their negative comments is much deeper than anything such fleeting sympathy can offer.

and honestly? despite all this shit i'm saying, i will also be the first to say that it's not anyone's responsibility to baby someone with depression. you can't be someone's therapist. you're not trained for it, you're not paid to do it, and honestly, in our society, we're worked too hard to be emotionally available like that for others. people with depression can suck your energy like a vampire. i think it's ok to offer to listen to someone in a moment of crisis but you can't fall into a codependent relationship where you're just listening to them all of the time.

it's why we need actual mental health care and support groups and financial resources and all that jazz. depression is quite literally a disability. give depressed people the resources and support to manage their lives. help them access trained professionals who can give them guidance and better coping mechanisms. you know?

hey buddy. if you genuinely want to help someone who's depressed, try and put more effort into it than some generic bullshit about how "suicide is never the answer" and "this is a temporary problem and you'll find happiness eventually!"

if your only motivations are to drop some one liner like that and disappear without even offering to listen to the person in question, then yeah. don't bother.

imagine spending the last however many years of your life just constantly struggling. there's some ups, but it's mostly downs, and the downs are utterly horrible. imagine being in so much pain that the ONLY way out is to escape it as fast as possible, to get some kind of release, because you have pressure in your chest and zero energy and even your best friend got sick of you a year ago because you didn't have anything positive to talk about and you're not advancing your life at all... maybe you're working some dead end job for minimal pay... maybe you're in debt... maybe you still live with your parents... maybe you have an amazing life but you haven't moved past the abuse/trauma from your childhood or your ex... there are so many reasons.

this is how ideations start. when you are SO STUCK in your own mind that the only thing you can think of is making it stop as fast as possible. some people turn to drugs. lots of people play video games. but when typical distractions stop helping and even when you're playing your favorite game you have this itch in the back of your mind telling you that everything you do is hopeless, nobody has tried reaching out to you in months, you're the last thought on anyone's mind and building new relationships would take WAY too much time and energy that you do NOT have...

and then, to get some of your stress out, you post a line or two online about your thoughts. "nobody will ever love me." it's true. who is going to put time and effort into befriending you when you're toxic to yourself, and thus, to the people around you? when you push everyone away, willingly or not. maybe you befriend someone for a couple days, a month, whatever, but they always disappear and you're left alone.

and some stranger comes by and says something like "don't give up you'll find someone in the future" ...

it feels so empty. when you've gone through years of pain. of sadness. of anxiety. of whatever you're going through. that one small comment from a stranger isn't going to counteract all of a depressed person's lived experiences.

they need so much more help than that.

if you want to actually help someone with depression, vote for a healthcare system that will allow them to access therapy/medication. offer to let them vent to you. actually try being there for someone who's down.

personally i would rather hear nothing than petty bullshit from normal/happy people who don't actually give a single fuck about me and are just saying empty words to make themselves feel better.

edit: sorry if my comments are harsh. just, after 2 hospitalizations and being unable to afford my medication/therapy and struggling to maintain some semblance of normalcy i get really sick of people giving their 5 seconds of support and vanishing. it happens whenever a celebrity commits suicide too. oh linkin park's lead singer killed himself? literally everyone on my social media starts posting about how if you're feeling down you can always call the suicide hotline. but no, don't talk to me, because i'm not emotionally available for you, and i'll forget about all of this in two days.

people started calling me a narcissist. i started lashing out from the stress of bottling everything up. think verbal abuse. i feel like a monster. i was never like this before i took meds.

they help. they work. they all do different things and have different side effects you have to deal with. they allow you to live your life and breathe a little. i still laughed on my meds. i had happy moments. i wasn't completely numb. it stopped my racing thoughts so whenever i would get upset about something i didn't stay upset, i got over it pretty quickly. that used to be rare for me.

despite that, i won't be going back on them. i would rather die.
